title: Capacity, Utilization, and Bottleneck Analysis
summary: Use multi-domain telemetry to identify the resource most likely limiting a synthetic workload.
objectives: Interpret CPU, GPU, memory, storage, network, power, and cooling signals together.
Distinguish utilization from failure and state uncertainty.

vocab.def: A constrained resource limiting performance or throughput.
The portion of a resource currently in use.
Unused modeled capacity available for variation.

sections.heading: High is not automatically bad
sections.body: High utilization may be expected when performance and service goals are met. Low utilization may still accompany a bottleneck elsewhere. Compare duration, capacity, workload, and outcome.

sections.heading: Use multiple signals
sections.body: A synthetic scenario may show high GPU use, normal network, memory pressure, and rising temperature. Evidence supports hypotheses, not automatic root-cause claims.

practice.prompt: Which resource is a likely bottleneck when GPU use is low, storage latency is high, and the data feed is slow?
practice.answer: The storage/data path is a likely constrained resource, subject to verification.

quiz.question: What is a bottleneck?
options: A constrained resource limiting performance or throughput
A reason to change production systems randomly
quiz.answer: A constrained resource limiting performance or throughput

criteria: Identifies a plausible constrained resource from evidence
States uncertainty without assuming highest utilization is failure

lab.objective: Identify a likely synthetic workload bottleneck.

futureCompetencyCandidates: analyze synthetic AI/cloud capacity and bottlenecks
